plain: To discourage someone from acting by fear of results.

webster.text: To discourage and stop by fear; to stop or prevent from acting or proceeding, by danger, difficulty or other consideration which disheartens, or countervails the motive for an act.

more.text: To prevent by prohibition or danger.

example.quote: No mischief, no misfortune, ought to deter us from a strict observance of justice and public faith.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 3, Virginia Convention, June 10, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
